science_goal: What mechanisms set the depth of a planet-carved gap in a protoplanetary disc? Varying planet mass, disc viscosity, and dust fragmentation velocity.

hypotheses.description: Fragmentation velocity sets the ratio of mm-continuum dust gap depth to gas gap depth by controlling the Stokes number of the largest grains and their trapping efficiency at the outer gap edge.
predicted_observables: delta_dust / delta_gas spans 2 orders of magnitude over v_frag = 1–10 m/s at fixed M_p = 0.5 M_Jup
factor >= 10 contrast in mm gap depth between inside and outside the water snowline for the same planet

hypotheses.description: Disc viscosity controls a threshold alpha* below which the outer gap edge exceeds the Rossby Wave Instability criterion, converting an axisymmetric dust ring into an azimuthal crescent observable at mm wavelengths.
predicted_observables: mm azimuthal intensity contrast transitions from C < 1.5 to C > 3 as alpha decreases through alpha* ~ 3e-4 for M_p = 1 M_Jup
dust crescent drifts in azimuth on timescale tau proportional to alpha^{-1}, detectable in multi-epoch ALMA imaging

hypotheses.description: Planet mass drives gap depth as M_p^2 in the sub-thermal regime, but super-Jupiter planets (> 2–3 M_Jup) excite eccentric Lindblad resonances that deepen the gap beyond the Kanagawa formula, potentially causing systematic bias in planet mass inferences from DSHARP-style observations.
predicted_observables: Gap depth vs. M_p follows Kanagawa power law for M_p < 2 M_Jup and flattens/deviates for M_p > 3 M_Jup
Break mass M_break scales as alpha^{0.5} * (h/r)^{2.5} if gap eccentricity drives the deviation

warnings: RWI threshold alpha* formula is inferred from scaling arguments — verify against Lovelace et al. 1999 and Li et al. 2000 [VERIFY IN ADS]
Kanagawa formula coefficients (0.04 prefactor) come from 2D isothermal hydro; 3D or non-isothermal corrections may shift thresholds by 20–30%
The M_break ~ alpha^{0.5} (h/r)^{2.5} scaling is a new analytical prediction from this session — not yet in the literature [VERIFY IN ADS before citing]
